phase3_invariant_proving.summary: PROOF SUCCESSFUL: The invariant 'gossip deduplication uses complete composite key (slot, proposer_index, index)' holds for all reachable code paths. The 96-byte composite key construction via computeCacheKey ensures perfect deduplication with no collisions for distinct tuples and guaranteed cache hits for identical tuples.
phase3_invariant_proving.invariant_statement: ∀ sidecars S1, S2: (S1.slot = S2.slot ∧ S1.proposerIndex = S2.proposerIndex ∧ S1.index = S2.index) ⟺ computeCacheKey(S1) = computeCacheKey(S2)
phase3_invariant_proving.proof_method: Symbolic execution over all code paths + key uniqueness theorem

proof_steps.claim: The cache key is a deterministic function of exactly three components: (slot, proposerIndex, index)
proof_steps.evidence: Code analysis of computeCacheKey (validate_data_column.go:233-238) shows key construction as Bytes32(slot) || Bytes32(proposerIndex) || Bytes32(index)
proof_steps.verification: Phase 1 abstract interpretation confirmed all three components are extracted and used

proof_steps.claim: Bytes32 encoding provides bijective mapping from uint64 to 32-byte arrays
proof_steps.evidence: bytesutil.Bytes32 performs fixed-width big-endian encoding. For any uint64 value v, Bytes32(v) produces a unique 32-byte representation. Two different values v1 != v2 produce different encodings Bytes32(v1) != Bytes32(v2).
proof_steps.verification: Mathematical property of fixed-width encoding with no hash collisions

proof_steps.claim: Concatenation of three 32-byte components preserves distinctness
proof_steps.evidence: If tuples (S1, P1, I1) != (S2, P2, I2), then at least one component differs. Due to fixed positions (bytes 0-31 for slot, 32-63 for proposerIndex, 64-95 for index), different tuples produce different concatenations.
proof_steps.verification: Phase 2 key uniqueness proof established this formally (phase2_symbolic_execution.key_uniqueness_proof)

proof_steps.claim: All code paths that check or mark duplicates use the same key computation
proof_steps.evidence: Gossip validation (line 153) and cache marking (subscriber:73) both call the same computeCacheKey function. RPC client path also uses setSeenDataColumnIndex which calls computeCacheKey.
proof_steps.verification: Phase 2 symbolic analysis of PATH-1-GOSSIP, PATH-4-RPC-REQUEST-SENT confirmed consistent key usage

proof_steps.claim: The deduplication check occurs before acceptance for all receiving paths
proof_steps.evidence: Gossip path checks at line 153 before further validation. RPC client path marks as seen after verification but before storage. No path can bypass this check.
proof_steps.verification: Phase 2.5 reachability analysis mapped all entry points and confirmed deduplication is on all receiving paths

proof_steps.claim: Therefore: Two sidecars with identical (slot, proposerIndex, index) will always be deduplicated
proof_steps.evidence: From steps 1-5: Same tuple → same key → cache hit on second occurrence → ValidationIgnore returned → second sidecar rejected
proof_steps.verification: Phase 2 equivocation test in PATH-1-GOSSIP demonstrated this behavior symbolically

formal_invariant_properties.safety: At most one data column sidecar with any given (slot, proposerIndex, index) tuple will be accepted and stored
formal_invariant_properties.liveness: A valid data column sidecar with a novel (slot, proposerIndex, index) tuple will eventually be accepted if it passes validation
formal_invariant_properties.uniqueness: computeCacheKey provides perfect bijection between (slot, proposerIndex, index) tuples and cache keys

additional_security_properties_proven.property: No cache key collisions for distinct tuples
additional_security_properties_proven.proof: 96-byte fixed-width concatenation with deterministic component encoding ensures distinct tuples produce distinct keys

additional_security_properties_proven.property: Consistent deduplication across gossip and RPC paths
additional_security_properties_proven.proof: Both paths use the same computeCacheKey function and seenDataColumnCache instance

additional_security_properties_proven.property: Different indices for same (slot, proposer) are correctly treated as distinct
additional_security_properties_proven.proof: Index is the third component of the key; different indices produce different cache keys

phase3_invariant_proving.notes: This is a mathematically sound deduplication mechanism. The use of a complete composite key prevents equivocation attacks where an attacker might try to send conflicting data for the same (slot, proposerIndex, index) tuple. The implementation is consistent with the Ethereum consensus specification and matches the pattern used for blob sidecar deduplication.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: No vulnerability found. The deduplication logic is correctly implemented and secure. Phase 2 found no counterexample, and Phase 3 successfully proved the invariant holds for all paths.

scope_analysis.note: While the code is in scope, there is no vulnerability to report

detailed_assessment.defense_in_depth_rationale: The deduplication mechanism sits downstream of multiple cryptographic validation layers (ValidProposerSignature, SidecarKzgProofVerified, SidecarInclusionProven). Even if deduplication were hypothetically bypassed, an attacker cannot inject conflicting data without the proposer's private key. The deduplication check prevents spam/replay attacks and ensures spec compliance, but is not the primary security boundary.
upstream_protections: ValidProposerSignature: Requires valid BLS signature from proposer's private key
SidecarKzgProofVerified: Requires valid KZG commitment proofs
SidecarInclusionProven: Requires valid merkle inclusion proof
Rate limiting: Gossip peer scoring and RPC rate limits prevent spam
